name: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅ decays
notes: The collaboration's own word is 'evidence'; the paper is not described as an observation.

significance.quote: providing the first evidence for this decay at $3.5$ standard deviations

summary.plain: Belle II reports the first evidence for a very rare B decay into a kaon and two neutrinos. Because the neutrinos leave no trace, the analysis uses the properties of the accompanying B meson in each collision. The paper says the combined result is 2.7 standard deviations above the Standard Model expectation.
summary.technical: Inclusive-tag analysis (B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.7 ± 0.5 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵) and an auxiliary hadronic-tag analysis ([1.1 +0.9/−0.8 (stat) +0.8/−0.5 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵) in 362 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S), combined to B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.3 ± 0.5 (stat) +0.5/−0.4 (syst)] × 10⁻⁵, 'the first evidence for this decay at 3.5 standard deviations'; the combined result is 2.7 standard deviations above the Standard Model expectation.

title: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ ν ν̅ decays
why_it_matters: B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅ is a flavour-changing neutral-current transition, suppressed in the Standard Model; the paper says its rate predictions are relatively precise and that the rate can be significantly modified in models with non-SM particles such as leptoquarks, or the B⁺ could decay to a kaon and an undetectable particle such as an axion or a dark-sector mediator. All earlier analyses found no evidence for a signal.
